item.title: New AI Development Tools Integrate Security at Build and Runtime
item.description:
New AI Development Tools Integrate Security at Build and Runtime

As AI accelerates software development, hidden complexity has become a more critical security challenge. A new approach combining clean, curated base images, runtime profiling, and automated vulnerability remediation addresses this by reducing unnecessary code and exposure. Organizations continuously ingesting open source software must verify, trust, and evaluate components as they move through development, testing, and production following Zero Trust principles.

#AIsecurity #Containers #Vulnerabilities #CI/CD #ZeroTrust

Source: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era

item.title: ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29
item.description:
ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29

ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to address three critical vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages.

🔍 Overview

  • Control Center Express is a central dashboard used by IT administrators to monitor and remotely manage fleets of PCs.
  • The product is marketed to businesses and IT service providers and supports more than 200 ASUS business, workstation, and Corporate Stable Model motherboards.

⚙️ Fixed Vulnerabilities

CVE Severity Type Impact
CVE-2026-114202 Critical (CVSS 10.0) Hard‑coded cryptographic key Unauthenticated remote attacker can forge an authentication token and gain administrator privileges with no prerequisites
CVE-2026-114204 Critical Hard‑coded key Remote attacker with low privileges can forge a session token for a recently logged‑in account
CVE-2026-114205 Critical Authorization flaw Low‑privileged user can create an administrator account

🚀 Availability

  • Versions earlier than v1.7.29 are affected. The security bulletin lists versions through v1.7.27; the status of v1.7.28 is unclear.
  • Affected users should install v1.7.29, then update agents on managed devices via Select Function → Client Agent Updater and verify the agent versions.

📦 Related Updates

  • Control Center Enterprise and Control Center Datacenter received patches for CVE-2026-126574, a critical authorization flaw that lets a low‑privileged Viewer role change an administrator’s password.
  • Armoury Crate was updated to fix CVE-2026-112115, a high‑severity privilege escalation flaw affecting all versions up to 6.7.2.

💡 Why it matters

  • The unauthenticated remote exploit (CVE‑2026‑114202) provides full administrative control without any user interaction, representing a worst‑case scenario for enterprise IT environments.
  • Even the lower‑privilege flaws could enable attackers to elevate their access, potentially compromising large fleets of managed PCs.
  • Prompt patching is essential to maintain the integrity of the management console and the devices under its control.

#ASUS #Security #Vulnerabilities #ITManagement

Source: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express

item.title: Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released
item.description:
Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released

On November 19, security updates were released for 18 vulnerabilities in the PHP development ecosystem, alongside the patching of a critical remote code execution flaw in the Drupal content management system. These updates address severe security issues that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable servers.

🚀 PHP Security Updates

The PHP dev team released updates for all supported branches, with versions 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available. Security firm Aikido reports that these updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP’s core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components. The most serious flaw, CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2. This vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM; standard configurations that do not reuse connections are not affected. As a temporary mitigation, administrators can disable persistent backend connections to ensure they are closed after each request. Third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has released patched packages for unsupported versions back to PHP 5.6, and Aikido has released hardened container images for similar unsupported versions.

🧩 PHP Vulnerability Details

The following vulnerabilities were fixed in the November updates:

CVE Identifier Description
CVE-2026-129474 Use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-126714 Vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files
CVE-2026-115560 Session serializer mismatch vulnerability
CVE-2026-129291 PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-128090 PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability

Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs. As a temporary mitigation for CVE-2026-115560, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0. This vulnerability was disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory.

🛡️ Drupal Critical Flaws

The Drupal Security Team has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165. Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, this flaw allows anonymous users to exploit the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, potentially leading to site takeover or remote code execution. The security team warned that at least one critical vulnerability can be exploited by anonymous users. Drupal administrators are urged to upgrade to versions 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13. For those who cannot immediately upgrade, it is recommended to secure the Drupal installer by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file. This update also addresses a moderately critical gadget chain vulnerability (CVE-2026-132166). The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged five Drupal vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild since November 2021.

#PHP #Drupal #SecurityUpdates #Vulnerabilities #CVE

Source: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs Source: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly

item.title: F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
item.description:
F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities

US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.

🔍 Overview

  • Status: NEW
  • Five stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) and BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature.
  • Unauthenticated threat actors can exploit these issues to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on vulnerable configurations.
  • F5 also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) caused by an integer underflow weakness.

🧩 How it works

  • Tracked vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637.
  • Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts during exploitation.
  • This is a data plane issue only with no control plane exposure.

🚀 Availability

  • F5 stated there are no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online.

💡 Why it matters

  • Although F5 has not flagged any of these issues as exploited in attacks, admins should upgrade systems quickly.
  • Cybercrime and nation-state threat groups have often abused F5 vulnerabilities in the wild to breach corporate networks, map internal servers, hijack devices, deploy data-wiping malware, and steal sensitive files.

#Cybersecurity #F5 #Vulnerabilities #Patch

Source: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
